title: Retain terminal direct output with the cancellation-entry remedy
question: Can terminal Run avoid the encoded snapshot while preserving publication and resource lifetimes?
summary: Retain scoped traffic/completion evidence and the isolated cancellation-entry remedy; withhold general activation.

workloads: Seeded plain partition -> probabilistic allocation, explicit one worker; fixed 20k/200k events and native resource controls.

validation.summary: Native and persistent-Chrome original-variant parity and storage controls remain scoped to those builds. The later cancellation remedy passes eight focused Linux scenarios; Windows/WASI acceptance of that revision is not inferred.

limitations: Small development cells and uncontrolled cache/background state do not establish general device, shape or tail performance.
Historical percentage gains are not additive; every comparison uses its own pinned baseline.
Snapshot and staging overlap shifts; lower temporary counters do not imply lower combined filesystem use.
The later revision has Linux validation only; general activation and broader workloads remain unproved.
exclusions: Storage/pressure diagnostics are not speed observations.
Original cancellation precedence is rejected; prior runtime acceptance does not validate the revised prototype.
reopen_when: Require a named completion or whole-job benefit question and validation of the actual revised variant before a promotion proposal.
